note: '1.5 GJ heat ... per tonne of clinker' for chemical absorption. Per t CLINKER. Carrier not stated - 'heat' for solvent regeneration, recorded as steam. 'This would result in a 50% increase of the energy need for clinker production.'

note: '0.2 GJ electricity (CO2 compression) per tonne of clinker'. Per t CLINKER.

source-original: 6.2 GJ natural gas per tCO2 captured
note: 'CO2 capture would require 6.2 GJ of natural gas per tCO2 captured. This is much more than the energy needed for CO2 capture in power plants.' Per t of CO2 CAPTURED (the unit of output of a capture unit), not per t of refinery product. The same study puts the total cost above $200/tCO2 (sidecar; no year, basis not stated).

'requires 0.28-0.30 kWh/Nm3 of low-pressure oxygen (about 0.8 GJ/tO2)' - the GJ/t figure is the source's own conversion (0.28-0.30 kWh/Nm3 at about 1.43 kg/Nm3 is 0.71-0.76 GJ/t, so 'about 0.8' is rounded up). High-pressure processes, PSA and ion transport membranes might cut energy and capital cost by 30% (sidecar).

'The energy needed for CO2 transportation and compression depends on distance and pressure. A typical value is between 0.2 GJ and 0.5 GJ of electricity/tCO2 (per 100-200 km).' Per t CO2 transported, per 100-200 km, INCLUDING compression.
